text:
mike: FYI started a quick thread after the morning deploy — p95 latency jumped on the web API after the kernel selector change. looks like prefill accounted for most of the regression. attaching profiler snippets below and some initial hypotheses.

nina: thanks. can you paste the perf numbers? is it cluster-wide or single model? :thinking_face:

mike: cluster-wide on the hosted pool for rwd-13b (quantized int8 path). sample from a 5m trace: 
```
overall p95: 290ms -> 430ms (post-change)
overall p99: 520ms -> 740ms
prefill median: 70ms -> 180ms
decode median: 90ms -> 110ms
prefill p95: 160ms -> 320ms
decode p95: 200ms -> 260ms
KV cache hit rate: 92% (stable)
microbatch size (configured): 8 -> autoscaled down to 4 on tail
```
The kernel selector flipped long-seq matmul to `fused_sgemm_v2` which profiles worse for our prefill patterns (many short prefix dims).

julia: interesting — prefill doubling is big. is the prefill work dominated by attention or the initial embedding/matmul? any flamegraphs?

mike: profiler says prefill is ~65% attention matmul's time + 25% kv/cache bookkeeping in our runtime (copy + key cache writes). decode time stayed roughly same but tail decode p99 did increase slightly. here's a simplified breakdown for a 256-token prefill and 64-token decode sample: 
```
prefill: total 180ms
  - token embedding & LM head: 15ms
  - attention matmul: 120ms
  - kv cache writes: 30ms
decode: total 110ms
  - attention matmul: 70ms
  - kv cache reads: 20ms
  - softmax / apply-out: 20ms
```
(note sums rounded)

sam: KV hit rate is 92% so cache isn't the primary cause. two hypotheses: 1) fused_sgemm_v2 is optimized for long contiguous matmuls but handles many small matmuls poorly (prefill has lots of different seq lengths in our prefix batching). 2) the kernel switch changed memory layout causing extra copies during KV writes.

perf-bot: automated perf-check: detected +48% p95 regression on rwd-13b-hosted since selector change. Regression window: 1711980000-1712000000. Possible culprit: kernel selection policy `prefers_fused_sgemm_v2` enabled.

nina: can we validate by forcing previous kernel on a canary subset? A/B to confirm. Also need to measure microbatching dynamics — the autoscaler stepping microbatch from 8->4 at tail seems harmful.

mike: did a quick canary: pinning to `matmul_v1` on 10% of hosts restored p95 to ~300ms. So selector flip looks causal. But we should also examine batching heuristics — when we drop microbatch size latency per request can increase due to fewer fused ops but throughput preserved. For tail, smaller microbatches reduce queueing but increase per-request overhead.

julia: let's think SLO tradeoffs: we have a 300ms p95 SLO for interactive endpoints. prefill-heavy requests (long prompts) are sensitive. Options: 
- revert selector globally (fast but blunt)
- refine kernel selector to prefer `matmul_v1` for prefill paths and `fused_sgemm_v2` for decode when seq_len < threshold
- keep selector and optimize KV write path (reduce copies)
- adjust microbatch sizing dynamically by prefix length and latency budget

sam: I ran microbenchmarks: for seq_len=256, microbatch=8 gives best throughput but p95 slightly above SLO. microbatch=4 reduces p95 by ~20% but drops throughput by 18%. so it's the classical latency vs throughput tradeoff.

mike: agree. also noticed tail latency at p99 is dominated by zippering: many requests with short prefixes get batched with long prefill requests causing stragglers. our current batching heuristic batches by arrival time and max_batch_tokens but doesn't shard by request seq_len.

nina: proposal: batch-by-length buckets with a small latency cap (e.g., bucket waits max 6ms). shorter sequences route to fast-fused kernels with smaller microbatch targets, longer sequences go to throughput-optimized kernels with larger microbatch targets. That avoids head-of-line blocking.

julia: good. quick simulation results? any numbers on tail improvements?

mike: simulated with trace replay (5k samples):
- current: p95 430ms, p99 740ms, throughput 1000 qps
- bucketed batching + kernel routing + microbatch tuning: p95 310ms, p99 480ms, throughput 920 qps
So p95/P99 recovered close to pre-change while losing ~8% throughput.

sam: that's acceptable for hosted API endpoints where latency is prioritized. For Dedicated customers we might expose an SLA knob to pick throughput vs latency.

perf-bot: note: quantization path interacts with kernels — some kernels have optimized int8 codepaths, others fall back to fp16 which can change mem footprint and eviction behavior. If we route by kernel we must ensure consistent numeric path.

nina: regarding KV behavior — the profiler indicated extra memcpy during KV writes when using fused_sgemm_v2: an intermediary layout conversion is happening. Short-term we can add an in-place conversion path for cache writes to avoid copy, but need caution for concurrency.

mike: planned quick actions: 
1) Can we A/B the kernel selector (10% pinned) — already done, confirm extended run for 2 hours and collect tail stats. owner: @mike.
2) Implement length-bucket batching + latency cap (simulation looks promising). owner: @nina + @sam.
3) Add kernel-aware microbatch policy: prefer small microbatch for short prefixes, larger for long workflows. owner: @julia.
4) Investigate the KV write copy path and add in-place conversion if safe. owner: @sam.
5) If regression persists, consider a rollback toggle exposed to infra to flip selector globally. owner: @mike.

julia: I can start on (3) — will add a policy module hooking into the router to compute target_microbatch = clamp(base * sqrt(seq_len/64), 2, 16) and a kernel hint. Want to prototype in staging.

sam: I'll profile the kernel codepaths for the int8 path and check where the memcpy happens. maybe a simple change in the kernel wrapper can avoid the copy when write buffer is pre-allocated.

mike: timeline: quick mitigation (A/B + routing rules) this week. medium (batcher rewrite + KV fix) next sprint. I'll hold off global rollback unless A/B shows no improvement.

ops-bot: deploy note: pinned canary applied to fleet subset rwd-hosted-02 at 1712003000. Telemetry stream enabled: /telemetry/rwd-13b/canary.

nina: one more thing — we need to update perf tests to include prefill-heavy synthetic traces (256-1024 prefix) and also mixed short+long mixes to catch these regressions earlier. adding as test item.

mike: agreed. @julia @sam please add testcases to perf harness. Also add a dashboard widget showing prefill vs decode time breakdown per model so we can catch shifts quickly.

julia: noted. I'll create the dashboard tile and add alerts for prefill fraction > 50% of total latency.

mike: solid. let's regroup tomorrow AM with A/B results. thanks all. :thumbsup:
